stories.title: Bitcoin nears $80,000 as weekend liquidity thins out
stories.summary: Bitcoin climbed toward $80,000 this week in its best run since 2023, wiping out billions of dollars in short bets along the way. Ether and solana rose too, pulled up by the rally. Rising US federal debt past $40 trillion has added to the debate over bitcoin's role as a hedge. Traders now watch for a test of $80,000 as weekend trading volumes typically drop.
stories.whyItMatters: A fast short squeeze paired with thin weekend liquidity can amplify price swings, so readers tracking this lane should expect higher volatility risk.
whatToWatch: Whether bitcoin holds a test of the $80,000 level over the weekend
Liquidity depth as weekend trading volumes typically thin
Follow-through moves in ether and solana
questions: Is the rally driven by macro factors or leveraged positioning?
Will thin weekend liquidity break the $80,000 level or trigger a reversal?

stories.title: Coldcard ships firmware update after $114 million bitcoin theft
stories.summary: Hardware wallet maker Coldcard released a firmware update following a $114 million bitcoin theft. The company said it used AI tools during its review and caught additional bugs as a result. The update also strengthens how the device generates seed phrases, the backup codes that protect a wallet's funds.
stories.whyItMatters: Seed generation flaws in hardware wallets can expose large holdings, so this matters to anyone who stores bitcoin in cold storage.
whatToWatch: Whether affected users apply the firmware update
Any further disclosure on how the $114 million theft occurred
questions: How did attackers access $114 million in the first place?
Were the newly found bugs already exploited before this fix?

stories.title: MANTRA token hits record low after exploit halts its blockchain
stories.summary: The MANTRA token fell 18% to a record low after an exploit forced its blockchain to halt. Both CoinDesk and Cointelegraph reported the token's drop alongside the shutdown. Details on the exploit's size and cause remain limited.
stories.whyItMatters: A blockchain halt after an exploit raises questions about the protocol's security and hits holder confidence directly.
whatToWatch: When the MANTRA blockchain resumes operation
Further details on the exploit's cause and scope
Any recovery or compensation plan for affected holders
questions: Will the chain resume safely, or is a deeper fix needed?

stories.title: Solana cuts blockchain slot time to 350 milliseconds
stories.summary: Solana reduced its blockchain slot time to 350 milliseconds. The change is a technical upgrade aimed at speeding up how fast the network processes transactions.
stories.whyItMatters: Faster slot times can strengthen Solana's position for trading and other applications that need low latency.
whatToWatch: Network stability in the weeks after the change
Validator adoption of the new slot time
questions: Does the faster slot time raise any risk of network instability or validator centralization?

stories.title: Bitcoin miners' AI spending outpaces revenue 15-to-1
stories.summary: Bitcoin miners are pouring billions of dollars into AI infrastructure, but their AI capital spending now outpaces AI revenue by 15 to 1. Analysts say miners are using AI as a hedge, but it may not cover the risks miners actually face.
stories.whyItMatters: A hard pivot into AI capex changes miners' risk profile and could affect their valuations and bitcoin production plans.
whatToWatch: Whether AI revenue starts to close the gap with spending
Upcoming miner earnings reports for capex detail
questions: What risk are miners actually trying to hedge with AI investment?
Does AI spending protect miners from the risks that matter most to them?

stories.title: Laser Digital wins Japan's first crypto exchange approval in four years
stories.summary: Nomura-backed Laser Digital received approval to operate a crypto exchange in Japan. It is the first such approval Japan has granted in four years.
stories.whyItMatters: A major bank-backed firm entering Japan's crypto market signals renewed regulatory openness in a key Asian market.

stories.title: BTCS repaid Aave debt with ethereum, ended Q2 with $317,000 in cash
